letters-to-his-children: Theodore Roosevelt the Rough Rider and president was also a devoted, playful father, as these letters prove. He writes to his children about bear hunts and birds' nests, White House pets and family jokes, in a warm, boyish voice. The collection shows the human side of a larger-than-life figure — tender, funny, and endlessly curious.
advice-to-a-mother-on-the-management-of-: Victorian physician Pye Henry Chavasse wrote this famous manual to guide mothers through feeding, illness, and the daily care of infants and children. Immensely popular in its day, it was the Dr. Spock of the 1800s — though its advice now reads as a fascinating mix of wisdom and period error. A revealing look at how our great-grandmothers raised babies.
canada-for-gentlemen: James Seton Cockburn writes for the British sportsman and settler with an eye on Canada — its hunting, fishing, farms, and wide-open chances. Sound tips mix with warm praise of the young Dominion's promise. A lively guidebook from the days when Canada was calling young Englishmen west.
bonnie-prince-charlie-a-tale-of-fontenoy: G. A. Henty's Jacobite adventure follows a young hero through Fontenoy and Culloden alongside Bonnie Prince Charlie. Battles, narrow escapes, and Highland loyalty fill this stirring tale of the Forty-Five. History's romance at full Henty throttle, written for boys who loved a hero.
the-angel-adjutant-of-twice-born-men: Minnie Carpenter, a Salvation Army officer, recalls Kate Lee — the Angel Adjutant — whose work among the poor of London won countless souls. A tribute to a saint of the slums. Warm, earnest, and deeply moving. Her tireless love for London's poorest won her the name of angel, and countless grateful hearts.
marching-men: Sherwood Anderson's early novel follows Beaut McGregor, a young laborer who dreams of leading marching men to a new order. The author's brooding power is already at work. A strange, strong book from the writer of Winesburg, Ohio. His dream of disciplined workers marching toward a new day haunts this strange, powerful early novel.
kathleen: Christopher Morley, the beloved essayist, tells of Kathleen in this gentle novel — a story of youth, books, and the charm of everyday life. His warm, bookish humor glows throughout. A delightful minor work from a major charmer. College days, first love, and literary talk fill this warm, gentle story of youth.
celtic-tales-told-to-the-children: Louey Chisholm retells Celtic tales for children — Cuchulain, Fionn, Deirdre, and the old heroes of Ireland and Scotland. Her clear, lively versions open the Celtic world to young readers. Enchanting stories, beautifully and simply told. Giants, fairies, and heroes step gaily through her pages.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aachen: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia piece on Aachen — Charlemagne's city of the great cathedral — covers its past, its shrine, and its kings. Joseph Lins keeps the facts straight and the story clear. A handy, solid reference on a famous old German town.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-sain: This article treats Saint-Ouen of Rouen, famed for its soaring Gothic church. The monks' pride still lifts Norman eyes. Gilbert Huddleston recounts its past. A crown of stone over Rouen. Its great organ is famed throughout Normandy. Its tower crowns the Rouen skyline.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-wald: The Encyclopedia's Waldsassen entry: the Bavarian Cistercian house of the famous library. Wood and gold frame its book hall. Edmond Obrecht gives its history. A jewel of the Oberpfalz. Its basilica glitters with southern German Baroque. Its nuns keep the old Cistercian rule.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aberdeen: This 1913 reference article on Aberdeen — the Scottish diocese, old and new. John Joseph A'Becket traces its bishops through penal days. The granite city's Catholic story, told with care. Scotland's north-east in church history. Its bishop hid priests in the penal times.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-contzen: This 1913 reference article on Adam Contzen — the Jesuit confessor of Maximilian of Bavaria. Benedict Guldner sketches his influence. He steered a prince through the Thirty Years' War. A confessor behind the throne. His books attacked the Protestant princes. The war years tested his counsel.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-of-breme: This 1913 reference piece on Adam of Bremen — the chronicler of the northern lands. Arthur Remy praises his Gesta of Hamburg's bishops. Vikings, missions, and Vinland fill his pages. The first historian of Scandinavia. His book lights the dark north. His Vinland passage proves the Norse reached America.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agen: This 1913 reference piece on Agen — the French diocese of the Garonne valley. Georges Goyau gives its history. Its cathedral honors St. Caprais. Bishops have ruled here since Roman days. A venerable see of Aquitaine. Its bishops faced the Revolution's storms.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albert-of-aac: This 1913 reference piece on Albert of Aachen — the chronicler of the First Crusade. Thomas Shahan weighs his vivid history. Godfrey's host marches through his pages. His tale shaped the crusading legend. The crusade's first historian. His Latin is vivid and credulous.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-nam: This 1913 reference article on Alexander — the name of seven men in Scripture. Anthony Maas sorts each mention. Maccabees and Gospels share the name. The entry aids the Bible reader. Seven bearers, one famous name. Their stories span both Testaments. Their names recur in the lectionary.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alphonse-magn: A 1913 entry on Alphonse Magnien — the Sulpician of Baltimore. Cardinal Gibbons honors his seminary work. St. Mary's formed priests under him. His learning served the American Church. A Frenchman for the American clergy. His philosophy classes drew the brightest. His memory lives in Baltimore's halls.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-screen: A 1913 entry on the altar screen — the rood screen of the old churches. Augustin Schulte describes its carved partition. The rood loomed above its loft. East and West both raised such walls. The sanctuary's carved veil. Its loft once held the singing boys.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amen: A 1913 entry on Amen — the Church's word of assent. Herbert Thurston traces its liturgical use. So be it seals every prayer. The faithful answer with one voice. The shortest creed in Christendom. Its Hebrew root means firm and true. Its echo closes the canon's prayer.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arnold-jansse: A 1913 entry on Arnold Janssen — the founder of the Divine Word Missionaries. Herman Richarz honors his Steyl foundation. His sons preach in every land. The missions' great organizer. The father of the Steyl family. His society spans the five continents.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baden: A 1913 entry on Baden — the German grand duchy's church story. Joseph Lins traces its sees. The Kulturkampf tested its bishops. The Black Forest guards its spas. A land between the faiths. Its casinos drew the European elite. Its grand duke ruled from Karlsruhe.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baron-ernst-v: This 1913 reference piece on Ernst von Feuchtersleben — the physician poet of Vienna. Arthur Remy honors his Diätetik der Seele. His verses taught the care of souls. The empire's doctors read his pages. A healer of body and mind. His aphorisms are still quoted.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baron-guillau: This 1913 reference article on Guillaume Dupuytren — the great French surgeon. James Joseph Walsh honors his fearless knife. His contracture bears his name still. Paris's hospitals knew his skill. The first surgeon of his age. His museum preserves the specimens. His Hôtel-Dieu ward was famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baron-von-mun: This 1913 reference article on Münch-Bellinghausen — an Austrian statesman of note. Arthur Remy records his career. The entry preserves his modest fame. The empire's service knew his zeal. A figure of the imperial age. His dispatches fill the state archives.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedict-van-: A 1913 entry on Benedict van Haeften — the Benedictine of the spiritual way. Michael Ott honors his Regia via crucis. His books guided the devout. The cloister prized his counsels. A monk of the interior life. His Schola cordis formed the devout.
